name: Colorado

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Chardonnay, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc and Sémillon fully without cooking off their freshness.
Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Riesling is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water. Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 5°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
